language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

<margin>Volume <term>Wa</term> <gloss>sixteenth volume marker in the Tibetan-Mongolian index</gloss>, Various Sutras, Two</margin>
of an unobstructed nature. Holding single-pointed
mindfulness, give rise to the thought of beholding
the <term>Tathāgata</term> <gloss>Thus-Come One, an epithet of the Buddha; Mongolian: činaγsi iregsen</gloss>.
Come hither, O son of good family <note>original: "ijaγur-tan-u kübegün", translating Sanskrit "kulaputra"</note>!
With a single-pointed mind, you
shall behold right before your eyes the <term>Tathāgata</term> <gloss>Thus-Come One</gloss>
Buddha of the auspicious direction.
In this way, when guarding oneself and when
the son of good family goes toward the direction of
the Buddha, the <term>Tathāgata</term> <gloss>Thus-Come One</gloss>,
the Truly and Completely Enlightened Buddha <note>original: "ünen tegüs tuγuluγsan burqan", translating Sanskrit "samyaksaṃbuddha"</note>, shall make
mountains and cliffs, as well as rivers and waters, disappear,
and shall deliver him from suffering.
Therein, through the blessing of the Buddha, the unevenness
of the ground shall be cleared away and made level.
In this way, whichever direction
he may go, even though there be no guide to show
the path, and no one to give instruction,
he shall enter upon the right path, and rightly
<margin>Various Sutras <note>original: "諸品經"</note>, Scroll Two, Upper Part, Folio Two</margin>

<summary>This folio from the Mongolian Buddhist canonical collection "Various Sutras" (ele jüil) instructs a practitioner ("son of good family") on cultivating single-pointed mindfulness to behold the Buddha. Through the Buddha's blessing, physical obstacles such as mountains and rivers vanish, uneven ground is made level, and the practitioner finds the true path even without a guide.</summary>
